pg008_n0007: This text book, Bible Knowledge for Secondary Schools Student’s Book has been written specifically for Form One students in the United Republic of Tanzania.
pg008_n0008: It has been written in accordance with the 2023 syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education.
pg008_n0009: The book consists of four chapters, namely: The concept of the Bible and Bible knowledge, God’s creation, the fall of man and the formation of the Patriarchs in the Bible.
pg008_n0010: Each chapter contains activities and exercises.
pg008_n0011: You are encouraged to do all the activities and exercises, as well as other assignments that your teacher will provide.
pg008_n0012: However, for excellent performance and for the acquisition of competencies expected from the study of Bible Knowledge, you are required to read the Bible thoroughly according to the syllabus.

pg009_im008: Introduction text explaining that the Bible is God’s word to humankind and outlining the chapter’s focus on the Bible, Bible Knowledge, Genesis, related subjects, and the importance of applying biblical teaching in daily life.
pg009_n0010: The Bible is the word of God to humankind.
pg009_n0011: The Word of God has been granted to people in different times and languages.
pg009_n0012: The Bible has a message for human salvation and sustainability.
pg009_n0013: Salvation is a gift to man through faith as revealed in the Bible.
pg009_n0014: God instructs man through the Bible.
pg009_n0015: Therefore, in this chapter, you will learn about the concept of the Bible and Bible Knowledge, the classification of the books in the Bible, the concept of the book of Genesis, the relationship between Bible Knowledge and other subjects, and the importance of learning Bible Knowledge.
pg009_n0016: The competencies developed will enable you to explain the meaning of the Bible, Bible Knowledge and its importance, such as to know God’s will, solving daily life challenges, maintaining peace with others, being united with God, building the spirit of faithfulness to God and living responsibly in the society and ultimately having an eternal life.
pg009_n0020: The word ‘Bible’ comes from a Greek word biblion, which means a book.
pg009_n0021: In its plural biblia, which means books.
pg009_n0022: There are several definitions of the Bible, some of them are highlighted as follows:
pg009_n0023: The Bible is a collection of Sacred Writings.
pg009_n0024: It is the Christian scriptures, consisting of the Old and New Testaments.
pg009_n0025: It is a book like no other.
pg009_n0026: The Bible is the Word of God, giving the message to humankind concerning the history of our Salvation.
pg009_n0027: Therefore, the Bible is the word of God through which He is directly speaking to human being and the creation.
pg009_n0031: Bible Knowledge is a subject that deals with the knowledge about God.
pg009_n0032: It deals with accurate studying, understanding, observing, interpreting and applying biblical facts into daily life.
pg010_n0005: The concept of knowledge from the Bible
pg010_n0007: According to the book of Genesis, God placed a tree of knowledge of good and evil in the Garden of Eden and commanded Adam and Eve not to eat fruits from the tree.
pg010_n0008: However, they both chose to disobey God (Genesis 3:1-6).
pg010_n0009: Adam and Eve knew intellectually about good and evil because of the commandment of God.
pg010_n0011: Remember that good knowledge is what God wants us to know and believe.
pg010_n0012: In the garden, Eve decided to believe in evil knowledge, which is what Satan wanted her to know and believe.
pg010_n0013: As a Bible student, you are instructed to examine and meditate on the word of God.
pg010_n0014: Satan always tries to trick people (Jeremiah 17:9 & John 10:10).
pg010_n0016: The Bible has so much to say about knowledge, both good and evil.
pg010_n0017: It teaches that creation reveals the knowledge of God (Psalm 19:1-2).
pg010_n0018: Sometimes, human knowledge can cause pride and grief in society.
pg010_n0019: Remember, God’s knowledge comes from fear of the Lord (Proverbs 1:7).
pg010_n0021: Relationship between Bible Knowledge and other subjects
pg010_n0023: Bible Knowledge relates with many subjects for their direct applications in human life.
pg010_n0024: Bible Knowledge relates somehow with Mathematics, Biology, History, Geography, Civics and languages.
pg010_n0025: Like other subjects, Bible knowledge is concerned with the nature of reality, meaningful life and obedience to God.
pg010_n0029: Mathematical principles are used in daily life such as in counting people, things and places.
pg010_n0030: Considering Bible Knowledge principles in the Book of Numbers, the Israelites were counted by Moses to get the number of men above 20 years who could go to war (Numbers 1:1-3).
pg010_n0031: Although the Bible does not offer an advanced study of mathematics, yet the Book of Numbers points to the relevance of mathematics in the community.
pg010_n0035: Both Bible Knowledge and Biology deal with the origin of life.
pg010_n0036: Although the Bible does not provide a detailed study of Biology, it does however recognise that God is the ultimate source of all life.
pg010_n0037: Reproduction is taken to be God’s command in the Bible, where He instructed everything he created to multiply and be fruitful.
pg010_n0038: Indeed, procreation must be regarded as a process of recreating and subduing the life-giving Earth for the growth of God’s nations (Genesis 1:28).
pg011_n0007: History tells the record of past events or where we came from, where we are, and where we are likely to go.
pg011_n0008: Biblical facts and narratives are explained historically.
pg011_n0009: Both Bible Knowledge and History explain past events in different times and places, as well as the ways in which past events inform the present life.
pg011_n0013: Both Bible Knowledge and Geography describe the origin and caring for the universe (Genesis 1).
pg011_n0014: Biblical Geography is the study of Bible lands, and the examination of places and features that are within the boundaries of those lands.
pg011_n0018: Civics is the study of the theoretical and practical aspects of citizenship as well as its rights and duties:
pg011_n0019: The duties of citizens to each other as members of a political body and to the government.
pg011_n0020: The principles of the Bible and civics deal with human beings’ life, centered in the laws as guidance in their daily lives.
pg011_n0021: Without laws, human guidance will not be easy.
pg011_n0022: God knew that the Israelites in the wilderness needed laws as guidance to their journey towards the Promised Land (Exodus 20).
pg011_n0023: Civics also teaches civil laws as guidance in the rule of law.
pg011_n0027: Language is a means of communication.
pg011_n0028: The Bible uses different languages to communicate the message of salvation to humankind.
pg011_n0029: Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek were the major early biblical languages.
pg011_n0030: Recently, English, Kiswahili, French and other languages, and even dialects have become among the languages of the Bible.
pg011_n0031: Therefore, Bible Knowledge helps to improve language skills.

pg012_n0007: Different people were inspired by the Holy Spirit to write the Bible.
pg012_n0008: This process took about 1,500 years to be completed.
pg012_n0012: Canonical books comprise a set of an official list of sacred writings accepted by Jews and Christian communities as the revealed word of God.
pg012_n0013: The number of books in the Bible varies depending on traditions.
pg012_n0014: The Catholic Bible has 73 books, in the sense that the Old Testament has 46 books and the New Testament has 27 books.
pg012_n0015: The number of books in the Bible according to Protestant Churches, is 66; with 39 books in the Old Testament and 27 books in the New Testament.
pg012_n0019: The Bible is broadly divided into two parts: The Old Testament (OT) and the New Testament (NT).
pg012_n0023: The Old Testament describes the origin of the universe, the roots of evil and the history of salvation through the history of the Israelites.
pg012_n0024: The Old Testament was written before the birth of Jesus Christ (BC).
pg012_n0026: The Old Testament is centered on a few great facts, such as creation of the universe and the fall of man; God's promises to Abraham, the Sinai covenant, the kingdom with kings acting as God’s representatives, God's intervention to his people through the prophets, the exile and the restoration.
pg012_n0030: The New Testament tells us about the birth, life, teachings, suffering, death, resurrection and ascension of Jesus Christ, and the birth and spread of the Early Church.
pg012_n0034: Language is one of the important medium of communication in society.
pg012_n0035: Several languages were used to write the Holy Bible.
pg012_n0036: The Old Testament was first written in Hebrew and Aramaic.
pg012_n0037: Later, the Old Testament was translated into Greek.
pg012_n0038: The Greek translated version is commonly known as the Septuagint (LXX).
pg012_n0040: The New Testament was written in Greek.
pg012_n0041: Thereafter, the whole Bible was translated into Latin.
pg012_n0042: This Latin version is called Vulgate.
pg012_n0043: From Latin translation, the Bible was translated into other languages.
pg013_n0004: The style of writing in the Bible
pg013_n0006: The Bible was written in different styles such as narratives, poems, sayings, stories, letters, proverbs, songs, prayers, sermons and prophecies.
pg013_n0008: The purpose of writing the Bible
pg013_n0010: The Bible was written for different purposes such as warning, teachings, corrections, and insights (2Timony 3:16).
pg013_n0014: We get so many benefits from studying Bible Knowledge.
pg013_n0015: The following are some of them: The study of Bible knowledge helps the learner to develop critical thinking and improve communication skills.
pg013_n0016: Again, it helps the learner to get the correct understanding of the scriptures.
pg013_n0017: Moreover, it helps us to get knowledge from the Bible and put it into practice in life.
pg013_n0018: Furthermore, the study of Bible knowledge aids us to know our divine origin and destination, and to get insight on how to acquire eternal life.
pg013_n0019: Still the study of Bible knowledge helps us to know God.
pg013_n0020: “And this is eternal life, that they know you the only True God and Jesus Christ whom you sent” (John 17:3).
pg013_n0021: It also supports us to have good relationships with others, to be servant leaders in society and avoid corruption (Exodus 18:21; 1 Samuel 12:3; Hosea 9:9) eventually to be responsible citizens.
pg013_n0022: Last but not the least, the study of Bible knowledge prepares the learner for further biblical studies.

pg017_n0021: The Concept of the Book of Genesis
pg017_n0023: The Book of Genesis is the first book in the Bible.
pg017_n0024: It is divided into two main parts, with chapters 1-11 telling the story of God and the whole world, and chapters 12-50 focusing on the story of God, a man and his family.
pg017_n0026: The word Genesis is a Greek word, which means ‘Origin’ or ‘Birth’ or ‘Beginning’.
pg017_n0027: Genesis or Bereshit in Hebrew, explains the origin of the universe, human race, as well as the origin of sin, suffering and death.
pg017_n0028: It also describes the origin of the Jewish people, and how God intervened to repair the damage caused by sin.

pg022_n0005: The concept of mankind being created in God’s image
pg022_n0007: The concept of mankind being created ‘in the image of God’ has its roots in Genesis 1:26-27, wherein “God created man in his own image…”
pg022_n0008: This scriptural passage does not mean that God is in human form, but rather, that humans are in the image of God in their moral, spiritual, and intellectual nature.
pg022_n0010: In the Bible, God can be sad, hurt, angry or joyful – the same emotions that human beings have.
pg022_n0011: We make choices and decisions every day.
pg022_n0012: God also makes choices and decisions.
pg022_n0013: Human beings were created with unique abilities embodied from God who is the source of what we are.
pg022_n0014: Essentially, the idea of being created in the image of God involves the following points:
pg022_n0017: God is intellect (God is intellectual Being) while man has intellect.
pg022_n0018: Therefore, man participates in God’s intellect.
pg022_n0019: No other creature has intellect except human being.
pg022_n0020: Intellect is the faculty of reasoning and understanding objectively, especially with regard to abstract matters.
pg022_n0021: The human mind is always searching for truth.
pg022_n0024: Consciousness is the state of being aware of and responsive to one’s surroundings.
pg022_n0025: Awareness is an activity of the mind.
pg022_n0026: To be aware is to be able to follow God’s conscience where man responds through prayers and good acts.
pg022_n0029: Will power is an ability to control one’s own thoughts, actions, and emotions.
pg022_n0030: This ability is granted only to human beings.
pg022_n0033: Free will is the capacity of human beings to make choices and decisions.
pg022_n0034: Subjectively, human decisions are made based on experiences, freedom, and choices.
pg022_n0035: Human choices are determined by two fundamental principles of life, that is: what is right and what is wrong.
pg022_n0036: When one chooses good or right, he/she chooses God.
pg022_n0039: Subduing is the act of bringing things under control.
pg022_n0040: The human being has been given this power by God to control God’s creatures.
pg022_n0041: This power is entrusted only to human kind.
pg022_n0044: Speaking is an act of conveying information (verbal expression) or expressing one’s feelings in speech.
pg022_n0045: Animals do not have that capacity.
pg022_n0046: Only humankind can communicate feelings or thoughts by speaking.
pg022_n0047: Speaking is a special gift granted to human beings.

pg045_n0017: The tower of Babel in biblical literature was a structure built in the land of Shinar (Babylonia) sometimes after the flood. The story of its construction, given in Genesis 11:1-9, appears to be an attempt to explain the existence of diverse human languages. According to Genesis, the Babylonians wanted to make a name for themselves by building a mighty city and a tower with its top in the heavens. God disrupted the work by confusing the language of the workers that they could no longer understand one another. The city was never completed, and the people were dispersed over the face of the earth. Therefore, it was called Babel, because there the Lord confused the language of all the earth; and from there the Lord scattered them abroad over the face of all the earth.” In this view, Babel means confusion. pg074_n0042: Two years later, Pharaoh had the following dreams: He was standing by the river Nile.

pg074_n0049: Then, the thin ears of corn swallowed the full ones.
pg074_n0050: The following morning, Pharaoh commanded all his magicians and wise men to interpret the dreams, but they failed.
pg075_n0004: Joseph was brought in and he interpreted the dreams as a warning of the prosperous years to come in Egypt.

pg075_n0012: The symbols of power given by Pharaoh to Joseph

pg077_n0007: Reconciliation of Joseph and his brothers (Genesis 45:1-28)
pg077_n0009: Joseph could no longer control himself before all those who stood by him, and he cried, “Make everyone go out from me” (Genesis 45:1).
pg077_n0010: So, no one stayed with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
pg077_n0011: And he wept so loudly such a way that the Egyptians and the household of Pharaoh heard it.
pg077_n0012: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph; is my father still alive?” (Genesis 45:3).
pg077_n0013: His brothers were dismayed at his presence.
pg077_n0014: He spoke to them assuring that what they did was a plan of God for him to serve their lives.
pg077_n0015: He told them to go and tell their father to make haste to come to Egypt and live in the land of Goshen.
pg077_n0017: When the report was heard that Joseph’s brothers had come, it pleased Pharaoh.
pg077_n0018: Pharaoh told Joseph to tell Jacob and his family to come and live in the land of Egypt.
pg077_n0020: In response to Pharaoh’s invitation for Jacob and his family, Joseph gave the following provisions to bring Jacob to Egypt.
pg077_n0021: First, he gave wagons to bring his father and family members, and made provisions for the journey.
pg077_n0022: Second, he gave a set of garments to each of the families.
pg077_n0023: Third, he gave 300 shekels of silver and five sets of garments to Benjamin.
pg077_n0024: Fourth, he sent ten donkeys to Jacob loaded with good things of Egypt.
pg077_n0025: Finally, he sent ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread and provision for Jacob’s journey.
pg077_n0026: At last, Joseph insisted them by saying, “Do not quarrel on the way” (Genesis 45:24).
pg077_n0028: When Jacob saw his sons and the convoy, he fainted for he did not believe when he saw the wagons, his spirit revived and he said, “It is enough; Joseph my son is still alive; I will go and see him before I die” (Genesis 45:28).

pg078_n0029: Jacob’s farewell message to his sons
pg078_n0031: Jacob called his sons and said, “Gather yourselves together that I may tell what shall befall you in days to come.”

pg078_n0033: Jacob implored his sons to bury him at Machpelah, for it was the place where his ancestors were buried.
pg078_n0035: Machpelah was a piece of land on the east of Mamre in Canaan.
pg078_n0036: It was bought by Abraham from Ephron the Hittite.
pg078_n0037: It was the burial place of Abraham and his descendants.
pg078_n0038: The following people were buried there: Sarah, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah and Jacob.
pg078_n0039: After speaking to them, Jacob died and was gathered to his people.
pg078_n0040: He was 147 years when he died.

pg009_n0010_easy_read: The Bible is God's word to all people.
pg009_n0011_easy_read: God gave His word to people at different times and in different languages.
pg009_n0012_easy_read: The Bible has a message about human salvation and sustainability.
pg009_n0013_easy_read:
Salvation is a gift from God.
People receive it through faith, as the Bible shows.
pg009_n0014_easy_read: God teaches people through the Bible.
pg009_n0015_easy_read:
In this chapter, you will learn about:
- the meaning of the Bible and Bible Knowledge
- the groups of books in the Bible
- the meaning of the book of Genesis
- the relationship between Bible Knowledge and other subjects
- the importance of learning Bible Knowledge
pg009_n0016_easy_read:
The skills you develop will help you explain:
- the meaning of the Bible
- Bible Knowledge
- the importance of Bible Knowledge
It will also help you to:
- know God's will
- solve daily life challenges
- keep peace with others
- be united with God
- build faithfulness to God
- live responsibly in society
- finally, have eternal life
pg009_n0020_easy_read:
The word ‘Bible’ comes from the Greek word biblion.
It means 1 book.
pg009_n0021_easy_read:
The plural word is biblia.
It means books.
pg009_n0022_easy_read:
There are several meanings of the Bible.
Some of them are given below:
pg009_n0023_easy_read: The Bible is a collection of Sacred Writings.
pg009_n0024_easy_read:
The Bible is the Christian scriptures.
It has the Old Testament and the New Testament.
pg009_n0025_easy_read: The Bible is a special book.
pg009_n0026_easy_read:
The Bible is the Word of God.
It gives people the message about the history of our salvation.
pg009_n0027_easy_read:
So, the Bible is the word of God.
Through the Bible, God speaks directly to human beings and creation.
pg009_n0031_easy_read: Bible Knowledge is a subject about knowing God.
pg009_n0032_easy_read:
Bible Knowledge involves:
- careful study
- understanding
- observing
- interpreting
- applying facts from the Bible in daily life
pg010_n0007_easy_read: In the book of Genesis, God put the tree of knowledge of good and evil in the Garden of Eden. God told Adam and Eve not to eat fruit from that tree.
pg010_n0008_easy_read: But Adam and Eve both chose to disobey God (Genesis 3:1-6).
pg010_n0009_easy_read: Adam and Eve knew about good and evil because God had given them this command.
pg010_n0011_easy_read: Remember this: good knowledge is what God wants us to know and believe.
pg010_n0012_easy_read: In the garden, Eve chose to believe evil knowledge. This is what Satan wanted Eve to know and believe.
pg010_n0013_easy_read: As a Bible student, you should study and think deeply about the word of God.
pg010_n0014_easy_read: Satan always tries to trick people (Jeremiah 17:9 & John 10:10).
pg010_n0016_easy_read: The Bible says a lot about knowledge, both good and evil.
pg010_n0017_easy_read: The Bible teaches that creation shows the knowledge of God (Psalm 19:1-2).
pg010_n0018_easy_read: Sometimes, human knowledge can cause pride and grief in society.
pg010_n0019_easy_read: Remember: knowledge from God comes from fear of the Lord (Proverbs 1:7).
pg010_n0023_easy_read: Bible Knowledge is linked to many subjects because it is used directly in human life.
pg010_n0024_easy_read:
Bible Knowledge is linked in some way with these subjects:
- Mathematics
- Biology
- History
- Geography
- Civics
- languages
pg010_n0025_easy_read:
Like other subjects, Bible Knowledge is about these things:
- the nature of reality
- a meaningful life
- obedience to God
pg010_n0029_easy_read: People use mathematical principles in daily life. For example, they use them to count people, things, and places.
pg010_n0030_easy_read: In the Book of Numbers, Moses counted the Israelites. He counted the men above 20 years who could go to war (Numbers 1:1-3).
pg010_n0031_easy_read: The Bible does not give an advanced study of mathematics. But the Book of Numbers shows that mathematics is important in the community.
pg010_n0035_easy_read: Bible Knowledge and Biology both deal with the origin of life.
pg010_n0036_easy_read: The Bible does not give a detailed study of Biology. However, it recognises that God is the ultimate source of all life.
pg010_n0037_easy_read: In the Bible, reproduction is God's command. God told everything He created to multiply and be fruitful.
pg010_n0038_easy_read: Indeed, procreation should be seen as a process of recreating and subduing the life-giving Earth for the growth of God's nations (Genesis 1:28).
pg011_n0007_easy_read: History records past events. It tells us where we came from, where we are, and where we may go.
pg011_n0008_easy_read: People explain biblical facts and stories through history.
pg011_n0009_easy_read: Bible Knowledge and History both explain past events in different times and places. They also show how past events help us understand life today.
pg011_n0013_easy_read: Bible Knowledge and Geography both describe the origin of the universe and how to care for it (Genesis 1).
pg011_n0014_easy_read: Biblical Geography is the study of Bible lands. It also studies the places and features inside those lands.
pg011_n0018_easy_read: Civics is the study of citizenship. It includes its ideas, its practice, and its rights and duties:
pg011_n0019_easy_read: These are the duties of citizens to each other as members of a political body and to the government.
pg011_n0020_easy_read: The principles of the Bible and Civics are about human life. They focus on laws as a guide in daily life.
pg011_n0021_easy_read: Without laws, it is hard to guide human life.
pg011_n0022_easy_read: God knew that the Israelites in the wilderness needed laws to guide their journey to the Promised Land (Exodus 20).
pg011_n0023_easy_read: Civics also teaches civil laws as a guide for the rule of law.
pg011_n0027_easy_read: Language is a way to communicate.
pg011_n0028_easy_read: The Bible uses different languages to communicate the message of salvation to humankind.
pg011_n0029_easy_read: Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek were the main early biblical languages.
pg011_n0030_easy_read:
Recently, these have become some of the languages of the Bible:
- English
- Kiswahili
- French
- other languages
- even dialects
pg011_n0031_easy_read: So, Bible Knowledge helps to improve language skills.

Different people wrote the Bible.

Canonical books are the official list of sacred writings.
Jews and Christian communities accept these writings as the revealed word of God.
pg012_n0013_easy_read: The number of books in the Bible changes with different traditions.
pg012_n0014_easy_read:
The Catholic Bible has 73 books.
The Old Testament has 46 books.
The New Testament has 27 books.
pg012_n0015_easy_read:
The Bible in Protestant Churches has 66 books.
The Old Testament has 39 books.
The New Testament has 27 books.
pg012_n0019_easy_read:
The Bible has 2 main parts:
- The Old Testament (OT)
- The New Testament (NT)
pg012_n0023_easy_read:
The Old Testament describes:
- the origin of the universe
- the roots of evil
- the history of salvation through the history of the Israelites
pg012_n0024_easy_read: The Old Testament was written before the birth of Jesus Christ (BC).
pg012_n0026_easy_read:
The Old Testament is about a few main facts:
- the creation of the universe
- the fall of man
- God's promises to Abraham
- the Sinai covenant
- the kingdom, with kings acting as God's representatives
- God's help to his people through the prophets
- the exile
- the restoration
pg012_n0030_easy_read:
The New Testament tells us about:
- the birth of Jesus Christ
- the life of Jesus Christ
- the teachings of Jesus Christ
- the suffering of Jesus Christ
- the death of Jesus Christ
- the resurrection of Jesus Christ
- the ascension of Jesus Christ
- the birth of the Early Church
- the spread of the Early Church
pg012_n0034_easy_read: Language is one important way people communicate in society.
pg012_n0035_easy_read: Several languages were used to write the Holy Bible.
pg012_n0036_easy_read: The Old Testament was first written in Hebrew and Aramaic.
pg012_n0037_easy_read: Later, people translated the Old Testament into Greek.
pg012_n0038_easy_read: The Greek translation is commonly called the Septuagint (LXX).
pg012_n0040_easy_read: The New Testament was written in Greek.
pg012_n0041_easy_read: After that, people translated the whole Bible into Latin.
pg012_n0042_easy_read: This Latin version is called Vulgate.
pg012_n0043_easy_read: From the Latin translation, people translated the Bible into other languages.
pg013_n0006_easy_read:
The Bible was written in different styles:
- narratives
- poems
- sayings
- stories
- letters
- proverbs
- songs
- prayers
- sermons
- prophecies
pg013_n0010_easy_read:
The Bible was written for different purposes:
- warning
- teaching
- correction
- insight
(2Timony 3:16)
pg013_n0014_easy_read: Studying Bible Knowledge gives us many benefits.
pg013_n0015_easy_read:
Some benefits are:
The study of Bible Knowledge helps the learner to think carefully and communicate better.
pg013_n0016_easy_read: It also helps the learner to understand the scriptures correctly.
pg013_n0017_easy_read: It also helps us to get knowledge from the Bible and use it in life.
pg013_n0018_easy_read:
The study of Bible Knowledge also helps us to know our divine origin and destination.
It also helps us to understand how to get eternal life.
pg013_n0019_easy_read: The study of Bible Knowledge also helps us to know God.
pg013_n0020_easy_read: "And this is eternal life, that they know you the only True God and Jesus Christ whom you sent" (John 17:3).
pg013_n0021_easy_read:
It also helps us to:
- have good relationships with other people
- be servant leaders in society
- avoid corruption
- become responsible citizens
(Exodus 18:21; 1 Samuel 12:3; Hosea 9:9)
pg013_n0022_easy_read: Lastly, the study of Bible Knowledge prepares the learner for further Bible studies.

pg076_n0029_easy_read: When the steward caught up with them, the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
pg076_n0031_easy_read: So they tore their clothes. Each man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city. They all bowed to Joseph and asked him to let them be his slaves.
pg076_n0032_easy_read: Joseph refused. He wanted the brothers to go, except Benjamin, because the cup was found with Benjamin.
pg076_n0034_easy_read: Judah asked Joseph to let Benjamin go with them. Otherwise, their father would die of sadness.
pg076_n0035_easy_read: "How can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? I fear to see the harm that would come upon my father" (Genesis 44:34).
pg076_n0036_easy_read: Joseph decided to give his brothers 1 more final test. He wanted to find out how they felt about their brother Benjamin and whether they cared about him or not.
pg077_n0005_easy_read: Explain why reconciliation is important in society.
pg077_n0009_easy_read: Joseph could no longer control himself in front of all the people standing near him. He cried, "Make everyone leave me" (Genesis 45:1).
pg077_n0010_easy_read: So no one stayed with Joseph when he told his brothers who he was.
pg077_n0011_easy_read: He cried so loudly that the Egyptians and Pharaoh’s household heard him.
pg077_n0012_easy_read: Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?" (Genesis 45:3).
pg077_n0013_easy_read: His brothers were shocked to see him there.
pg077_n0014_easy_read: Joseph spoke to his brothers. He assured them that what they did was God’s plan, so that he could save their lives.
pg077_n0015_easy_read: Joseph told them to go and tell their father to come quickly to Egypt and live in Goshen.
pg077_n0017_easy_read: When Pharaoh heard that Joseph’s brothers had come, he was pleased.
pg077_n0018_easy_read: Pharaoh told Joseph to tell Jacob and his family to come and live in Egypt.
pg077_n0020_easy_read: After Pharaoh invited Jacob and his family, Joseph gave them what they needed to bring Jacob to Egypt.
pg077_n0021_easy_read: First, Joseph gave them wagons to carry his father and family members. He also gave them what they needed for the journey.
pg077_n0022_easy_read: Second, Joseph gave each family a set of clothes.
pg077_n0023_easy_read: Third, Joseph gave Benjamin 300 shekels of silver and 5 sets of clothes.
pg077_n0024_easy_read: Fourth, Joseph sent Jacob 10 donkeys loaded with good things from Egypt.
pg077_n0025_easy_read: Finally, Joseph sent 10 female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and supplies for Jacob’s journey.
pg077_n0026_easy_read: At last, Joseph told them strongly, "Do not quarrel on the way" (Genesis 45:24).
pg077_n0028_easy_read: When Jacob saw his sons and the wagons, he fainted because he did not believe them at first. But when he saw the wagons, he felt strong again and said, "It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die" (Genesis 45:28).
pg077_n0029_easy_read: Reconciliation and unconditional forgiveness are powerful tools. They help rebuild the community and bring people together.
pg077_n0031_easy_read: Joseph’s unconditional forgiveness of his brothers points to the forgiveness of Jesus Christ in the New Testament.
pg077_n0032_easy_read: So, Christians learn that they should forgive other people. They should always be ready to forgive those who wrong them.
pg077_n0036_easy_read: Jacob, also called Israel, started the journey with everything he had.
pg077_n0037_easy_read: When Jacob reached Beer-sheba, he offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac.
pg077_n0038_easy_read: At Beer-sheba, God spoke to Israel in a vision at night. God said, "Jacob, Jacob... I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you a great nation.
pg077_n0039_easy_read: I will go down with you to Egypt. I will also bring you up again. And Joseph’s hand will close your eyes" (Genesis 46:2-4).
pg078_n0005_easy_read: From Beer-sheba, the sons of Israel carried their father Jacob, their children, and their wives in the wagons.
pg078_n0006_easy_read: They also took their cattle and their goods, and they reached Egypt.
pg078_n0007_easy_read: All the people from Jacob's family who went to Egypt were his own children and grandchildren. The wives of Jacob's sons were not counted. The total was 66 people.
pg078_n0008_easy_read: So, the total number of Jacob's household that came into Egypt was 70.
pg078_n0010_easy_read: In Egypt, Jacob lived in Goshen. Goshen was the best part of the land in Egypt.
pg078_n0011_easy_read: Pharaoh gave this land to Jacob, Joseph's father, and to all Jacob's descendants who moved to Egypt.
pg078_n0012_easy_read: Goshen is very close to the city of Rameses.
pg078_n0013_easy_read: Jacob lived in Egypt for 17 years.
pg078_n0014_easy_read: Jacob lived for 147 years in total.
pg078_n0018_easy_read: When Joseph heard that his father was ill, Joseph brought his 2 sons to Jacob. The sons were Ephraim and Manasseh.
pg078_n0019_easy_read: When Jacob saw Ephraim and Manasseh, he told Joseph what God had told him at Luz about giving him the land. Then Jacob said, "Ephraim and Manasseh are mine, just like Reuben and Simeon."
pg078_n0020_easy_read: Jacob told Joseph how Rachel died in Canaan on the way to Ephrath, that is Bethlehem.
pg078_n0022_easy_read: Then Jacob kissed Joseph's sons and hugged them.
pg078_n0023_easy_read: Jacob put his right hand on Ephraim, the younger one, and his left hand on Manasseh.
pg078_n0025_easy_read: Joseph tried to stop Jacob, but Jacob refused to stop blessing them.
pg078_n0026_easy_read: Jacob said that Ephraim would become great, and his descendants would become many nations.
pg078_n0027_easy_read: Jacob gave Joseph 1 portion more than his brothers.
pg078_n0031_easy_read: Jacob called his sons and said, "Come together. I will tell you what will happen to you in the days to come."
pg078_n0032_easy_read: Jacob told them what could happen to each of them, starting with Reuben and ending with Benjamin.
pg078_n0033_easy_read: Jacob begged his sons to bury him at Machpelah, because his ancestors were buried there.
pg078_n0035_easy_read: Machpelah was a piece of land east of Mamre in Canaan.
pg078_n0036_easy_read: Abraham bought it from Ephron the Hittite.
pg078_n0037_easy_read: It was the burial place of Abraham and his descendants.
pg078_n0038_easy_read:
The following people were buried there:
- Sarah
- Abraham
- Isaac
- Rebekah
- Leah
- Jacob
pg078_n0039_easy_read: After Jacob spoke to them, he died and was gathered to his people.
pg078_n0040_easy_read: Jacob was 147 years old when he died.
pg078_n0042_easy_read: Joseph ordered his servants, the physicians, to embalm Jacob for 40 days.
pg078_n0043_easy_read: All the Egyptians wept for 70 days.
pg078_n0044_easy_read: After the days of weeping ended, Joseph asked Pharaoh to let him go and bury his father, as he had been told to do.
pg078_n0046_easy_read:
Pharaoh allowed him. Joseph went with these people:
- all the servants of Pharaoh
- all the elders of Egypt
- all the household of Joseph
- all Joseph's brothers
- all his father's household
- chariots
- horsemen
pg078_n0047_easy_read: It was a very large group.
pg079_n0004_easy_read: When they came to the threshing floor of Atad beyond the Jordan, they cried loudly and with deep sorrow.
pg079_n0005_easy_read: Joseph mourned his father for 7 days.
pg079_n0006_easy_read: When the people of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, "This is great mourning by the Egyptians."
pg079_n0007_easy_read: So the place was called Abel-Mizraim.
pg079_n0008_easy_read: Joseph went back to Egypt with all his brothers and all the people who had gone with him to bury his father.
pg079_n0012_easy_read: When Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they became afraid. They thought Joseph might take revenge.
pg079_n0013_easy_read: They sent Joseph a message asking for pardon, as their father Jacob had asked.
pg079_n0014_easy_read: Joseph cried when he received the message. He said to them, "Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?"
pg079_n0015_easy_read: "You planned evil against me, but God planned it for good. God did this so that many people could stay alive, as they are today" (Genesis 50:20).
pg079_n0017_easy_read: Joseph lived with his brothers until he saw Ephraim's children to the 3rd generation.
pg079_n0019_easy_read: Joseph said to his brothers, "I am about to die."
pg079_n0020_easy_read: "God will come to help you and bring you up to the land that he promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob" (Genesis 50:24).
pg079_n0021_easy_read: Joseph made the Israelites promise that when they left the land, they would carry his bones with them.
pg079_n0022_easy_read: Joseph died at the age of 110 years.
pg079_n0023_easy_read: His body was embalmed. It was kept in a coffin in Egypt.
pg079_n0027_easy_read: From Joseph's life and history, we learn that God is faithful to people who obey him.
pg079_n0028_easy_read: We also learn that God defends and protects people who put their hope in him.
pg079_n0029_easy_read: We also learn that sometimes suffering and torture prepare people for higher positions.
pg079_n0030_easy_read: Also, trustworthiness and faithfulness are very important in human life.
pg079_n0031_easy_read: Finally, we learn that good behaviour starts at home.
